exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Credentials In Files
exploitedBy.relevance: Secrets embedded in image layers are effectively credentials stored in files within the container image filesystem.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Unsecured Credentials
exploitedBy.relevance: Embedding secrets in image layers represents unsecured credential storage that can be extracted by adversaries.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Implant Internal Image
exploitedBy.relevance: Container images with embedded secrets can be implanted or distributed internally, exposing credentials through image layer inspection.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Malicious Image
exploitedBy.relevance: Without classification label enforcement, malicious or unvetted images can be deployed as there is no policy gate to verify image integrity or classification.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Encrypted/Encoded File
exploitedBy.relevance: The lack of encryption for image layers at rest is the inverse of this technique, exposing stored data that should be protected with encryption.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
exploitedBy.relevance: Unencrypted image layer storage highlights the absence of encryption controls that would otherwise protect data at rest from unauthorized access or ransomware impact.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Lifecycle-Triggered Deletion
exploitedBy.relevance: Absent retention and expiry policies directly relate to the lack of lifecycle-triggered deletion controls for image artifacts.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Data from Information Repositories
exploitedBy.relevance: Without expiry policies, stale images accumulate in repositories and can be accessed by adversaries to collect sensitive data from outdated artifacts.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Code Repositories
exploitedBy.relevance: Inadequate access control granularity for classified images in registries mirrors weak repository access controls that allow unauthorized data collection.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Transfer Data to Cloud Account
exploitedBy.relevance: Cross-border transfer of classified image data directly maps to transferring sensitive data to external or foreign cloud accounts.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Data from Cloud Storage
exploitedBy.relevance: Classified image data stored in cloud registries can be accessed and transferred across borders via cloud storage access.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: File Deletion
exploitedBy.relevance: Improper disposal without purging layer blobs means residual data remains after deletion attempts, failing the secure file deletion requirement.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Clear Persistence
exploitedBy.relevance: Failure to purge layer blobs during image disposal leaves persistent artifacts that adversaries or auditors could recover.
